summary: Some chatas animals cannot be brought and are left to die, like the baby or swap of a chatas. A lost chatas that is found with a blemish is left to die if the owner already got kapparah; if not, it is sold and he buys another.

chunks.en: The baby of a chatas,
chunks.st: The offspring of a sin offering

chunks.en: the swap of a chatas,
chunks.st: and the substitute for a sin offering,

chunks.en: and a chatas whose owner died,
chunks.st: and a sin offering whose owner has died shall be sequestered and left to

chunks.he: יָמוּתוּ. שֶׁעָבְרָה שְׁנָתָהּ וְשֶׁאָבְדָה וְנִמְצֵאת בַּעֲלַת מוּם,
chunks.en: are left to die. A chatas whose year passed, or that was lost and found with a blemish,
chunks.st: die. And with regard to a sin offering that is unfit for sacrifice because its first year from birth has passed, and a sin offering that was lost and when it was found, it was blemished,

chunks.en: if the owner already got kapparah,
chunks.st: if it was after the owner achieved atonement through sacrifice of another animal as a sin offering, the blemished animal

chunks.en: it is left to die, and it does not make a swap.
chunks.st: shall die, and it does not render a non-sacred animal exchanged for it a substitute.

chunks.en: We may not use it,
chunks.st: Furthermore, one may not derive benefit from any of these sin offerings ab initio,

chunks.en: but if someone did, it is not me'ilah.
chunks.st: but if one derived benefit from them, after the fact, he is not liable to bring a sin offering for misuse of consecrated items.

words.note: Using something holy for yourself, which needs a korban to fix.

chunks.en: If the owner did not get kapparah yet,
chunks.st: And if the lost animal was found and discovered to be unfit before the owner achieved atonement for his sin with a different animal,

chunks.en: it grazes until it gets a blemish,
chunks.st: it shall graze until it becomes blemished,

chunks.en: and is sold, and with its money he brings another,
chunks.st: and then it shall be sold. And he must bring another sin offering with the money received from the sale.

chunks.en: and it makes a swap,
chunks.st: And this animal renders a non-sacred animal exchanged for it a substitute,

chunks.en: and using it is me'ilah.
chunks.st: and one who derives benefit from this animal is liable for misusing it.

summary: If someone's chatas got lost and he brought another one, and then the first was found, it is left to die. If money for a chatas got lost and then found after he brought a chatas, the money is thrown into the Dead Sea.

chunks.en: If someone set aside his chatas and it got lost,
chunks.st: In the case of one who designates a sin offering, and the animal was lost,

chunks.en: and he brought another in its place,
chunks.st: and he designated another in its stead and sacrificed it,

chunks.en: and after that the first one was found,
chunks.st: and thereafter the first animal was found; that is a sin offering whose owner achieved atonement with another animal, and

chunks.en: it is left to die. If someone set aside money for a chatas and it got lost,
chunks.st: it shall be left to die. In the case of one who designates money for purchase of his sin offering, and the money was lost,

chunks.en: and he brought a chatas in its place,
chunks.st: and he designated an animal as a sin offering in its stead, and he sacrificed it,

chunks.en: and after that the money was found,
chunks.st: and thereafter, the money was found,
chunks.stMore: it is prohibited to derive benefit from the money, as the money attains the halakhic status of the sin offering that was to be purchased with it, and that sin offering would be left to die because the owner achieved atonement with another animal. Therefore,

chunks.en: it is thrown into the Dead Sea.
chunks.explain: So no one can use it.
chunks.st: he must take the money and cast it into the Dead Sea, from where it cannot be recovered.

summary: Many cases of a lost chatas or lost money: if it is found before he brings the new one, he uses both together to buy one chatas, and the rest goes to gift korbanos. The Sages say a chatas is left to die only if it is found after the owner already got kapparah.

chunks.en: If someone set aside money for his chatas and it got lost,
chunks.st: In the case of one who designates money for purchase of his sin offering, and the money was lost,

chunks.en: and he set aside other money in its place,
chunks.st: and he designated other money in its stead,

chunks.en: and before he could buy a chatas with it
chunks.st: and he did not manage to purchase a sin offering with that money

chunks.en: the first money was found,
chunks.st: before the original money was found,

chunks.en: he brings a chatas from both,
chunks.st: he should bring a sin offering from a combination of this original money and that money designated in its stead,

chunks.en: and the rest goes to gift korbanos.
chunks.st: and the remainder shall be allocated for communal gift offerings.

words.note: Korbanos bought for the mizbe'ach when it has nothing else.

summary: If a chatas got a blemish, it is sold and another is bought with its money. Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon says that if the new one was brought before the first was shechted, the first is left to die.

chunks.en: If someone set aside his chatas
chunks.st: In the case of one who designates a sin offering

chunks.en: and it has a blemish,
chunks.st: and the animal is blemished,

chunks.en: he sells it and brings another with its money.
chunks.st: he sells the animal and must bring another sin offering with the money received in its sale.

chunks.en: Rabbi Elazar the son of Rabbi Shimon says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Shimon, says:

chunks.en: If the second one was brought before
chunks.st: If the second animal is sacrificed before the first

chunks.en: the first was shechted,
chunks.st: is slaughtered for non-sacred consumption, the first animal

chunks.en: the first is left to die, since the owner already got kapparah.
chunks.st: shall be left to die. Although it was sold and rendered non-sacred, its status is now that of a sin offering whose owner already achieved atonement with another animal.
